title: Name the Layers in an AI Experience
summary: Separate the model from the interface, context, retrieval, memory, tools, policy, and runtime around it.
objectives: Distinguish a model from a chatbot, assistant, and copilot experience.
Attribute observed behavior to the responsible product or runtime layer.
Replace brand-wide claims with exact, version-scoped statements.
Record unknown behavior instead of guessing.

sections.title: A model generates; a product surrounds it
paragraphs: A model maps supplied input and context to generated output. A product can add an interface, instructions, retrieval, memory, tools, identity, policy, deterministic code, and an execution environment.
When a product searches, remembers, edits, or sends something, identify the component that performed that behavior. Do not transfer every product capability to the model name.

sections.title: Chatbot, assistant, and copilot describe different experiences
paragraphs: A chatbot is organized around conversational turns. An assistant helps a person complete tasks. A copilot is embedded in a work surface while a person remains responsible for direction and consequential decisions.
Any of these experiences can contain a deterministic workflow or agentic mode. The label alone does not prove who chooses the next step, executes tools, stores state, or approves effects.

sections.title: Describe the exact experience
paragraphs: Name the product surface, version or observation date, configuration, enabled tools, permissions, and journey. Then label each claim documented, tested, inferred, or unknown.
A provider family can contain a model endpoint, consumer assistant, coding agent, framework, and managed agent service with different classifications.
sections.callout: Classify the observed experience—not the logo.

sections.title: Unknown is an honest result
paragraphs: Missing documentation does not prove capability or absence. An untested feature is not tested evidence, and a marketing claim is not a runtime trace.
Record what would resolve the unknown: a first-party contract, controlled run, permission inspection, tool trace, state record, or accountable review.

activity.title: Map one familiar AI experience
instructions: Choose one exact AI product experience and record its surface, observation date, configuration, and enabled capabilities.
Map the model, interface, context, retrieval, memory, tools, policy, deterministic code, and runtime.
For each claimed behavior, record responsible layer, evidence kind, source, and unknowns.
Rewrite one provider-wide or marketing-led statement as an observable scoped statement.
evidence: A complete layer map with no behavior attributed only to a provider name.
A claim table that separates documented, tested, inferred, and unknown evidence.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which capability did you initially assign to the model but later locate in the surrounding product?

cues.text: Separate the generative model from every product and runtime layer around it.
Show the model nested inside interface, context, retrieval, memory, tools, policy, and runtime layers.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: An ordered text list names each layer, its owner, and the behavior it contributes. Reduced-motion mode shows all layers at once.

cues.text: Compare chatbot, assistant, and copilot as experience terms rather than autonomy guarantees.
Demonstrate an exact, dated, configuration-scoped claim.
Model how to preserve an unknown and name the evidence needed to resolve it.
Check whether the learner can move one unsupported behavior claim to unknown.
Guide learners through the layer map and scoped-claim rewrite.
Begin the check after the learner can attribute behavior without using a provider name as proof.

questions.prompt: What does a model classification establish?
choices: The component maps supplied input and context to generated output
The product can safely execute every proposed tool
The provider is agentic
The user approved all side effects
questions.explanation: A model is the generative component; execution, authority, state, and product behavior require separate evidence.

questions.prompt: A product is called a copilot. What can you conclude from the name alone?
choices: It is autonomous
It is multi-agent
It is positioned as embedded assistance; runtime behavior still needs evidence
It has no tools
questions.explanation: Copilot is a product term, not proof of a particular control loop or authority boundary.

choices: Every product from this provider is agentic
This dated product mode used a documented search tool under the tested configuration
Large models are always assistants
A tool-capable API executes every tool itself
questions.explanation: The statement identifies the exact mode, date, evidence, and configuration.

questions.prompt: What should happen when documentation does not resolve who stores state?
choices: Assume the model stores it
Mark the behavior unknown and identify needed evidence
Treat the product name as proof
Ignore state
questions.explanation: Unknown preserves the gap without inventing capability or absence.

questions.prompt: Why separate a model from its harness?
choices: To locate execution, policy, state, and authority accurately
To avoid recording sources
Because models never generate tool calls
Because every harness is deterministic
questions.explanation: The harness owns important runtime behavior that the model name alone cannot establish.
